items.title: Blue Jackets’ Mathieu Olivier out week-to-week with upper-body injury
items.summary: Olivier has three goals and three assists in 22 games this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images The Columbus Blue Jackets will be missing a physical presence in their lineup for the next while. According to The Athletic ‘s Aaron Portzline, winger Mathieu Olivier is out week-to-week with an upper-body-injury. Olivier, 29, left Columbus’ 3-2 loss to the New Jersey Devils on Monday with the injury. It’s unclear exactly when or how it occurred, but The Hockey Writers ‘ Mark Scheig suggested it could be something that he’s been dealing with for some time. The Quebec native has three goals and three assists for six points in 22 games this season. He also leads the team with 32 penalty minutes. Olivier went undrafted by the NHL, and instead joined the Nashville Predators ‘ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Milwaukee Admirals for the 2018-19 season following his five-year career in the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). Over four seasons in the Predators’ organization, Olivier played in 48 NHL games, notching three goals and four assists for seven points. In July of 2022, Olivier was traded to the Blue Jackets for a fourth-round draft pick. He has emerged as a full-time NHLer in Columbus, adding some scoring touch to his already established toughness. His career-best campaign came in the 2024-25 season with the Blue Jackets, when he registered 18 goals and 14 assists for 32 points in all 82 regular season games. He has compiled 46 goals and 45 assists for 91 points over 285 total games with Columbus. He has led the Blue Jackets in penalty minutes in three of the last four seasons. Olivier is in the second season of a six-year, $18 million contract . With 19 points through 23 games, Columbus sits in seventh place in the Metropolitan Division . items.title: Why Maple Leafs’ William Nylander is getting a power-play demotion
items.summary: Hiller has removed Nylander from the flank of the club’s top power-play unit, a position the elite offensive talent has essentially owned throughout his prime.
items.body: BOSTON — In the ongoing discussion of William Nylander ’s underwhelming performance this month, Jim Hiller once said that there are “different ways” to hold players accountable for poor play. The head coach of the Toronto Maple Leafs did not bench his superstar winger for so much as a shift after Nylander’s direct giveaway to Matthew Knies ended up costing his reeling team a win at home Saturday. But Hiller has removed Nylander from the flank of the club’s top power-play unit, a position the elite offensive talent has essentially owned throughout his prime. A shocking sight, to be sure, at Boston’s TD Garden Thursday, as Nylander took reps with the seldom-used second unit and Kirill Marchenko joined PP1. In the past, it would’ve been Gavin McKenna or, perhaps, John Tavares getting the PP2 bump. “I think it was supposed to happen last game, but I didn't really pick up on it,” said Nylander, interpreting his demotion as punishment for his mistake against Columbus. “So, we’ll see how long he keeps it like that for. Amid his slump, Nylander is also skating on Toronto’s third line, now centred by Marlies call-up Aatu Räty and flanked by energy bug Easton Cowan. Räty is generally used in the defensive zone, so expect Hiller to get Nylander some extra O-zone starts with other linemates. items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj fined for slewfoot on Avalanche’s Fedor Svechkov
items.summary: Xhekaj was ejected from the game for the play.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Montreal Canadiens suffered a 6-0 defeat at the hands of the Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday, but the total loss for Canadiens winger Florian Xhekaj, specifically, is just a bit larger. On Thursday, the NHL Department of Player Safety announced that they have fined Xhekaj $2,426.98, the maximum allowable amount under the collective bargaining agreement (CBA), for his trip of Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov during Wednesday’s game. The play in question occurred late in the third period when Svechkov had the puck in the Colorado zone, and Xhekaj checked him from the side while kicking out his right leg from behind and throwing him down in a clear and obvious slewfoot. Xhekaj, who has a goal and two assists for three points in 12 games this season, was assessed a match penalty and ejected from the game for the play. This came shortly after defenseman Arber Xhekaj, Florian’s brother, checked Avalanche defenseman Brent Burns from behind at the Colorado blueline, causing Burns to get up slowly from the ice while a giant scrum formed as multiple Avalanche players came to Burns’ defense. Burns would require stitches after the play, but is expected to be fine. It was a rowdy affair on Wednesday, even if the score was not competitive. There was a total of 57 penalty minutes assessed in the game, with the Xhekaj brothers accounting for 33 of them. This is the 22-year-old Florian Xhejak’s first instance of league-levied discipline. Arber Xhekaj, on the other hand, has been fined by the NHL on three seperate occasions. Wednesday’s loss was Montreal’s third in a row, but they still sit third in the competitive Atlantic Division with 32 points through 26 games. items.body: Register Login Rangers Recall Juuso Parssinen; Gabe Perreault Out With Injury By Brennan McClain | at November 26, 2026 1:32 pm According to a team announcement , the New York Rangers recalled forward Juuso Pärssinen from the Hartford Wolf Pack in the AHL. Unfortunately, Pärssinen’s call-up comes with some bad news. The Athletic’s Peter Baugh reported that forward Gabriel Perreault is expected to miss the next four to six weeks with a lower-body injury. Perreault, 21, is in his second full season with the Rangers. Last year, his rookie season, the former first-round pick scored 12 goals and 27 points in 49 games with a net-zero rating, while averaging 15:59 of ice time per game. Still, he had a relatively slow start to the campaign. 19 of his 27 points came after the calendar flipped to March. This season, Perreault is again averaging approximately one point every two games. Before the injury, the middle-six winger registered seven goals and 11 points in 24 games with a -2 rating, averaging 16:39 of ice time per game. However, it was a reverse pace from last year. Perreault scored seven points in October, but only has four in November. Regardless, even if he isn’t New York’s leading offensive talent, he is a big part of the team’s future. Given his recovery timeline, he won’t return to the lineup until Christmas, at the earliest. Meanwhile, Pärssinen has the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since last season. items.title: Devils’ Brenden Dillon suspended four games for illegal check to head
items.summary: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon won’t take the ice for the next handful of games.
items.body: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon received a four-game suspension on Thursday for an illegal hit to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk. Dillon was assessed a match penalty for the check during the first period of the Devils' shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game after the hit. Dillon forfeits $82,474.24 based on his average annual salary and under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. The money goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. On the play, Mateychuk skated through neutral ice and entered the zone before moving the puck to a teammate. Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a “high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable,” the NHL's department of player safety said in a video. Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness said after the game: "I’ve coached Dillon. He’s not a dirty player. He’s a hard player. He caught him in a bad spot, and that’s a bad hit. It is.” Bowness said Wednesday that he spoke with Mateychuk and the defenceman “feels fine.” Bowness added that “protocol will take over and we’ll go from there.”

items.title: Flames’ Nemec returns to New Jersey with no regrets, improved play
items.summary: Since leaving New Jersey, Simon Nemec is starting to find out how good he can be. Eric Francis talked to the standout young blue-liner ahead of his return to the city that drafted him.
items.body: NEW YORK – Simon Nemec didn't need to leave New Jersey to prove he could play in the NHL. He needed to leave New Jersey to find out just how good he could be. He doesn’t want to revisit the frustrations, rehash the circumstances that led to his departure from New Jersey, or turn Friday’s return to the Devils into some sort of referendum on who was right and who was wrong. And with a five-game point streak in his back pocket, the Calgary Flames defenceman has some pretty good evidence that the change of scenery he needed is paying off. “It's probably a better spot for me,” Nemec said of his new team. “I just feel better here, and I got more room to play, more room to grow, and that's what I wanted. “I'm thankful for what happened in New Jersey. I think it helped me a lot, especially on the mental side. But now I just don't want to open some stuff from the past.” Friday afternoon’s game at Prudential Center will be Nemec’s first against the team that selected him second overall in the 2022 NHL Draft, and subsequently traded him to Calgary last June. “It was home for almost four years, so it's definitely special,” said Nemec. Nemec plans to catch up with former teammate Ondrej Palat, now with the New York Islanders, whose family became close with him. But the bigger story is what has happened since Nemec landed in Calgary. items.summary: Nylander was replaced on Toronto’s top unit by the returning Kirill Marchenko during Thursday’s practice.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images It’s hard to say with much conviction, but things could, just maybe, be looking up for the Toronto Maple Leafs . After an embarassing nine-game losing streak, the Leafs finally got back in the win column with a 4-2 victory over the New York Islanders on Monday. Winger Kirill Marchenko, who has missed Toronto’s last 12 games with a lower-body injury, returned to practice on Wednesday and could be ready to go for the Leafs’ road game against the Boston Bruins on Friday. In Leafs-like fashion, however, even the positive development of Marchenko’s return isn’t without a hint of controversy. The Russian national assumed his role on Toronto’s top power-play unit during Thursday’s practice, meaning one of the players that had been on the top unit got bumped off. Somewhat shockingly, head coach Jim Hiller pulled star winger William Nylander to make room for Marchenko, leaving Auston Matthews, John Tavares, and Gavin McKenna as the other forwards on the unit. Speaking with the media following Thursday’s practice, Nylander shared his thoughts on his power-play demotion. “I told him I didn’t agree with it, but that’s okay,” he said. items.title: Even after missing out on Dylan Larkin, the Minnesota Wild should remain all-in
items.summary: The Wild can ill afford to waste what might be their final year with Quinn Hughes.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are in a tough spot. Just under a year after mortgaging a sizeable chunk of their future to land star defenseman Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks , the Wild seem no closer to signing the 27-year-old to a new contract. If anything, Wild general manager Bill Guerin sounds less and less confident each time he’s asked about the situation. And yet … from a hockey standpoint, the Wild haven’t given Hughes any reason not to sign with them. As of Thursday, they’re tied with the Carolina Hurricanes atop the NHL standings with 41 points. They’ve won 18 of 27 games this season, along with just four regulation losses. Right now, they have to be the odds-on favorites to come out of the Western Conference. Hughes has missed Minnesota’s last three games with an undisclosed injury, but it shouldn’t be long before he returns to the lineup — and when he’s played, the Wild have given him more freedom than ever. The 5’10” righty has already amassed 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games this season, good for second on the Wild in scoring. He’s also averaging a career-high 27:49 of ice time per game. When healthy, Hughes is right there with Cale Makar in the Norris Trophy race every single year, and Hughes will likely continue to be the standard against which all undersized puck-moving defense prospects are measured until the day he retires. He’s as elusive and dangerous as any player in the league. The Wild have a ton of money coming off the books after this season, and you can bet they’d love nothing more than to give most of it to Hughes. Guerin and Wild owner Craig Leipold already made a big statement last year by making Kirill Kaprizov the highest-paid player in the game, at least for a moment.

items.body: It’s American Thanksgiving. Do you know where your NHL team is? The U.S. holiday has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Put simply, clubs sitting in playoff position at this time of year have a roughly 75 per cent chance of remaining there by season’s end. While far from a perfect rule, it’s generally pretty accurate. Take the past two seasons, for example — of the 16 teams inside the playoff window at Thanksgiving in back-to-back years, 12 ultimately clinched a spot. The rate was higher in 2022-23 and 2023-24, with 13 sitting and staying in a playoff spot. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Hockey Hall of Fame announced Thursday that former NHL defenseman Zdeno Chara has been appointed to its selection committee . Chara, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2025, will replace fellow inductee Igor Larionov. The Hall of Fame selection committee has 18 members and each serves a 15-year term. “It’s a true honor to be asked to serve on the Hockey Hall of Fame Selection Committee,” said Chara. “This game has given me so much throughout my life, and I take seriously the responsibility of helping recognize the individuals who have shaped its history and legacy. I am grateful for this opportunity.” The New York Islanders selected Chara in the third round of the 1996 NHL Draft. Throughout his 24-year NHL career, he skated with the Islanders, Ottawa Senators , Boston Bruins and Washington Capitals . A Slovak native, he recorded 209 goals and 471 assists for 680 points and 2,085 penalty minutes. At 1,680 career regular-season games, he ranks seventh on the NHL’s all-time games played list, and is 36th in points among NHL defenders. He reached the 50-point mark three times in his career and recorded a career-high 19 goals in 2008-09. He also finished with 40 assists and 52 points in 2011-12. He also dressed in 200 playoff games, where he scored 18 goals and added 52 assists for 70 points. He captained the Bruins to a Stanley Cup championship in 2011 and helped them reach the Final in both 2013 and 2019. Chara won the Norris Trophy in 2008-09 and was a five-time finalist in his career. By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 9:39 am A fight between two willing players, or a response to a dirty hit, is part of how hockey polices itself and part of what makes it special. But something has changed in how players react to legal hits. The old approach was to spring into action after an egregious or illegal hit and, after a big clean hit on a teammate, remember the number and settle it later. Now the reflex is to go after the hitter the moment the whistle blows, often halfheartedly, whether the hit was clean or not. So have fights and scrums after clean hits become an issue? The numbers say they have, and the league has had a tool to deal with them for more than three decades. A Pro Hockey Rumors review of NHL play-by-play data from all 399 regular-season games through Nov. 25 found 110 fights. Forty-three of them, or 39.1%, came within 10 seconds of a hit that drew no penalty, with no faceoff in between. In 32 of those 43 fights, one of the combatants was the player who delivered the hit. The instigator penalty was called seven times in those 43 fights. Only eight instigator penalties have been called league-wide this season. In 28 of the 43, the responding team received no penalty beyond the matching fighting majors. The fights are only part of it. Another 60 unpenalized hits this season were followed by roughing calls but no fight. That’s 1.4 of those scrums for every fight after a legal hit, and none of them show up in fight totals. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources American Thanksgiving represents a fascinating point in the NHL season because the sample sizes are large enough to matter for struggling teams, yet the season is just young enough that it’s still possible to save it in rare cases. The most famous example: the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues, who named Craig Berube interim head coach in November and rose from dead last in the NHL standings as late as Jan. 2 to winning the Stanley Cup. Maybe a case study like that gives teams false hope, maybe not. But we do frequently see firings start to pop up around this time of year in the NHL. In 2023-24, we saw four head coach firings before the league reached its late-December holiday break. The 2024-25 season had four bench bosses axed between Nov. 19 and Dec. 26 alone. The first pink slip of 2025-26 came in mid-January. Recent history thus tells us it’s not too soon to run a temperature check of every seat in the league. items.summary: Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon will have a hearing with the NHL Department of Player Safety today for an illegal check to the head/interference on Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk, the league announced. items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon To Have Hearing For Hit On Denton Mateychuk By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 8:31 am Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon will have a hearing with the NHL Department of Player Safety today for an illegal check to the head/interference on Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk , the league announced . The league hasn’t said whether the hearing will be by phone or in person. A phone hearing would cap any suspension at five games, while an in-person hearing would allow for a longer one. The hit came at 12:54 of the first period of New Jersey’s 3-2 shootout win in Columbus last night. Dillon caught Mateychuk in the Devils’ defensive zone and got a five-minute major and a match penalty. That ended his night after four shifts and 3:23 of ice time. Mateychuk went down hard and did not return. Columbus head coach Rick Bowness said afterward that the former 12th overall pick was fine and that concussion protocol would take over. New Jersey killed off the major and won on Arseny Gritsyuk ’s shootout goal, improving to 17-8-0 on the season. Dillon has been here before. In February 2024, while with the Jets, he was suspended three games and forfeited nearly $61K in salary for an illegal check to the head of Penguins forward Noel Acciari , which also drew a match penalty. Last November, he was fined $5K, the maximum allowable under the CBA, for boarding Blackhawks forward Tyler Bertuzzi . He also served a one-game suspension with the Sharks in December 2017 for slashing Capitals defenseman Madison Bowey . Because more than 18 months have passed since his last suspension, Dillon isn’t considered a repeat offender under the CBA, which affects only how much salary he’d forfeit. items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj receives match penalty for slew foot
items.body: It was a chippy affair between the Montreal Canadiens and Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday night, and Florian Xhekaj was right in the middle of all of it. It culminated late in the third period, when the forward was handed a match penalty for slew-footing Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov, subsequently ending his night. The infraction happened with just over a minute remaining in the game as the Canadiens were down 6-0. The whistle had just sounded when Xhekaj tripped up Svechkov and was assessed an intent-to-injure penalty. That would be five of Xhekaj's 22 penalty minutes on the evening, as he was also assessed a 10-minute misconduct in the second period. A match penalty comes with an automatic ejection and review from the league. Florian wouldn't be the only Xhekaj to amass a fair few PIMs on Wednesday, as brother Arber — a Canadiens defenceman — wracked up 16 of his own. The brothers combined for 33 of the 42 total penalty minutes in this game. Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog wasn't thrilled with the antics of the Xhekaj brothers, telling reporters that they "have to use (their) head a little bit." "The Xhekaj brothers, they wanted to get involved so we'll see what's going to happen with that," Landeskog told reporters after the game . "I think for one of the most storied franchises and one of the most respected franchises in all of hockey, and you've got two guys doing that." Florian, who has played 17 career NHL games, has 54 penalty minutes. There will be no chance for revenge, though, on either side as Wednesday's match wrapped up the season series between the two inter-conference teams.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NHL Department of Player Safety announced New Jersey Devils defenseman Brendan Dillon will have a hearing Thursday for an illegal check to the head on Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk during their game Wednesday night. Dillon, 36, delivered the hit midway through the first period after Mateychuk crossed the Devils’ blue line and made a pass to Jack Williams. Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness, who coached Dillon during his time with the Winnipeg Jets , told reporters after the game he didn’t think he was a dirty player. “He’s a hard player, and he caught him in a bad spot,” Bowness said . “That’s a bad hit.” Dillion has a goal and assist with 37 penalty minutes in 16 games with the Devils in 2026-27. Through 16 NHL seasons, the New Westminister, B.C., native has 43 goals and 186 assists for 229 points and 1,051 penalty minutes in 1,072 career regular-season games. The Department announced that Dillon will have a hearing on Thursday for an illegal check to the head and interference against Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk in their game Wednesday. Dillon received a match penalty for the hit, which came in the first period as Mateychuk skated into the New Jersey zone after delivering a pass along the blue line. The Devils defenceman appeared to leave his feet to deliver the hit on Mateychuk, who had kept his eyes on the puck to his right. Mateychuk stayed on the Columbus bench through the second period, but didn't play in the frame and didn't come back out for the third. He entered concussion protocol after the game. Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness told reporters post-game that Mateychuk "feels fine" Dillon also received a five-minute major on the play. He had logged just 3:23 of ice time before the ejection in what ended as a 3-2 New Jersey shootout win. The 36-year-old was suspended for an illegal check to the head of Pittsburgh Penguins forward Noel Acciari in 2024.

items.title: Avalanche rout Canadiens behind two goals from Toews
items.summary: Devon Toews scored twice in a 1:33 span during the second period, Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 27 shots and the refreshed Colorado Avalanche beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-0 on Wednesday night.
items.body: DENVER — Devon Toews scored twice in a 1:33 span during the second period, Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 27 shots and the refreshed Colorado Avalanche beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-0 on Wednesday night. Artturi Lehkonen, Logan O’Connor, Martin Necas and Gabriel Landeskog also had goals for the Avalanche, who were back in action for the first time since a 4-0 win over Anaheim last Thursday. Colorado looked energized by the break, especially in the second period with a three-goal spurt. Colorado posted its third consecutive home shutout, with Blackwood responsible for two and Scott Wedgewood one. It's the second time in Avalanche history they have notched three straight home shutouts, according to NHL research. They also accomplished the feat in November 2001 behind Hall of Fame goaltender Patrick Roy. The Canadiens dropped to 0-2 since acquiring Dylan Larkin in a deal with Detroit. Jacob Fowler stopped 32 shots. Cale Makar had three assists in his return after missing three games with a lower-body injury. Colorado outscored Montreal 10-1 in the two meetings this season. The game turned chippy in the third. Florian Xhekaj drew a major near the end of the contest. Defenseman Brent Burns took a hit in the back from Arber Xhekaj late in the third period and momentarily stayed down on the ice before heading to the bench. Burns has played in 1,031 straight games. He's 33 away from tying the NHL’s streak for consecutive games held by Phil Kessel (1,064). Parker Kelly appeared to catch the blade of Arber Xhekaj's skate near his wrist after a hit in the corner during the second period. Kelly went to the locker room moments after the play but returned to the bench.

items.body: Forwards combine for four points in win against Senators after being out since early October SUNRISE, Fla. -- The Florida Panthers had the band back together for the first time in a long time Wednesday. Captain Aleksander Barkov and forward Brad Marchand returned to the lineup after each had played just two games this season due to injuries early in October. Both were instrumental in Florida’s 5-3 win against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena. Marchand, who had been out since injuring his left knee in a 2-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Oct. 6, assisted on three of the Panthers’ first four goals. “It was great to be out there, but even better seeing ‘Barky’ back again,” Marchand said. Barkov missed the entire 2025-26 season with a right knee injury only to injury his left knee in a 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 1, the Panthers’ second game of the season. He scored into an empty net for his team’s final goal Wednesday, helping the Panthers end the first-place Senators’ nine-game point streak (7-0-2) and pull within one point of second in the ultra-competitive Atlantic Division. “I feel like I got better once the game started going,” Barkov said. “The second, third period were better. Obviously it takes time to get used to playing against a really good team. There’s not much space on the ice. You have to kind of figure it out. But playing with good players and a good time made it easier for me to find my rhythm.” The game Wednesday was the first time the Panthers got to see the team they envisioned in the offseason when landed forward Brady Tkachuk in a trade with Ottawa and added goalie Jacob Markstrom in a trade with the New Jersey Devils, among other moves. items.body: Canadiens icon scored 544 goals with C.C.M. three-piece twig that helped 'revolutionize' game Maurice “Rocket” Richard is sitting in the Montreal Canadiens dressing room during the 1959-60 season, the last of his illustrious NHL career. The smiling superstar is turning revolutions of black friction tape over the thick blade of his heavy wood stick for team photographer David Bier. It is a ritual the greatest goal-scorer of his generation had done many hundreds of times; on this occasion, his sons Maurice Jr. and Normand are witness to it in the Montreal Forum dressing room. This classic photo was published as part of a six-page Oct. 29, 1960 “Perspectives” newspaper supplement retrospective written by Le Soleil editor Guy Fournier, the Rocket having announced his retirement six weeks earlier. He had served as captain his final four seasons, winning the Stanley Cup in each of them, his eighth career championship having come in 1960. A 1942 newspaper advertisement for C.C.M. sticks, and Maurice Richard in front of a Montreal Forum stick rack, having just been named captain of the Canadiens for the 1956-57 season. One of the intriguing things about this snapshot of history -- apart from Rocket’s battered knuckles -- is the stamp on the wide, flat blade the Canadiens icon is about to cover with tape. It reads: “PATTERN MADE BY … EXTRA SPECIAL,” with C.C.M. stick-maker Ernie Evernden’s signature between the capital letters. This Wisconsin rock elm stick, very popular in the day, was a C.C.M. Pattern-Made Professional from the stock at long-ago Raymond Hardware, a regular Canadiens supplier, located about 3 miles from the Forum. items.body: Adam Fox and Brandon Montour are using the platform their NHL fame provides to bring awareness and fundraising to a personal cause that in a perfect world wouldn't exist at all. Fox, a New York Rangers defenseman, and Montour, a Seattle Kraken defenseman, know too well the impact of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, the currently incurable nervous system disease known as ALS. Fox's father-in-law is 62-year-old former NFL linebacker Tim Green, who has been living with ALS since 2016. Montour's brother, Cameron, died from the disease on Oct. 20, 2025, seven weeks shy of his 35th birthday, leaving behind wife, Chelsey, and daughters Peyton and Parker. Unified by their personal experiences, Fox and Montour are working with a coalition born out of ALS Action Canada called Courage to Fight ALS to bring awareness about the disease, to tell their personal stories associated with it, to raise money toward finding a cure, and to promote it across the NHL. "We're connected through this thing," Fox said. "It's not in a very pleasant way, but it's nice to have someone to try to build this with." Fox and Montour are of course quite busy with their regular jobs. Fox and the Rangers play in the Thanksgiving Showdown game against the Chicago Blackhawks at United Center on Friday (5:30 p.m. ET; HBO MAX, truTV, TNT, SN+). Montour and the Kraken play in Edmonton later Friday (8 p.m. ET; SN, KONG, Prime Video). But they are each giving much of their personal time toward the fight against ALS, also known as Lou Gehrig’s Disease. Since the start of last season, Fox, who wears No. 23, has been donating $1,023 for every goal he scores and $523 for every assist to Tackle ALS, the initiative that Green, who played eight seasons with the Atlanta Falcons, started jointly with the Sean M. items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, TJ Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior writer Amalie Benjamin profiles Amanda Kessel.
items.body: Triumph of returning to win Olympic gold so moving ‘they should do a movie about it’ The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, TJ Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior writer Amalie Benjamin profiles Amanda Kessel. The idea of winning that gold medal, of the United States coming back in the third period, tying the game on a goal by Monique Lamoureux-Morando, the distillation of all she had worked so hard to attain, brings that joy. She radiates that happiness through the phone, as she talks about the triumph at the 2018 Winter Olympics in PyeongChang, South Korea, about attaining what she had so long dreamed about, something that almost slipped through her fingers. As she put it, “It’s your life’s work with your best friends.” For so long, a gold medal had seemed almost a given, with Kessel’s talent and her work ethic, her speed and vision. Then came the concussion that almost derailed everything, the miraculous comeback that allowed her to restart a career that had seemed in the past. “The story of her coming back from basically retirement is … they should do a movie about it, honestly,” former University of Minnesota women’s hockey coach Brad Frost said. “It’s one of those types of stories.” Kessel will enter the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 induction class , with the ceremony taking place on Nov. 30 in Washington D.C. She will be inducted alongside her brother, Phil , as well as T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. items.body: The Montreal Canadiens lost a key piece of their blue line on Wednesday night. Defenceman Kaiden Guhle exited Wednesday's game against the Colorado Avalanche after suffering an apparent injury and the team announced that he would not return. While the nature of the injury is unclear, Guhle exited after getting hit from behind by Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog, then got tangled up with the forward in front of the net on the same shift, with both players falling to the ice. He did not return to the ice after the shift midway through the second period. Guhle had played 10:53 of ice time before leaving and had two shots on goal with a minus-1 rating. Blake Coleman had two goals and Bobby Brink also scored for the Western Conference-leading Wild (18-4-5), who were a franchise-best 12-0-3 in their previous 15 games. After Coleman cut the deficit to one with 4:04 left, Mammoth center Barret Hayton was whistled 19 seconds later for a double-minor penalty for high-sticking Joel Eriksson Ek. The Wild had a power play for the remainder of regulation but managed only two shots. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for his first win in seven starts since Oct. 24 and Lawson Crouse and Dmitri Simashev scored for the Mammoth, whose second-period leads of 3-1 and 4-2 gave the Wild a two-goal deficit for the first time since their last regulation loss at Calgary on Oct. 22. Crouse’s tip-in of Vincent Trocheck’s shot in the first period stopped Minnesota’s scoring-first streak at 15 straight games. That was tied for the second-longest run in NHL history and best in the league since Montreal in 1972. The Canadiens have the record with 18 consecutive games, set during the 1959-60 season. Kirill Kaprizov’s franchise-record streak of 15 straight games with a point ended, as did his run of six consecutive games with multiple assists. That was the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind Wayne Gretzky's eight in 1984. Kaprizov went without a point for just the third time in 27 games, with linemates Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy also producing at a prolific rate this season. The Wild played without star defenseman Quinn Hughes for the third straight game with an undisclosed injury.

items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first American to score 21 goals in 14 games
items.body: Only three full seasons into his NHL career, Cutter Gauthier is rewriting record books. The Anaheim Ducks star forward has been on a near-unparalleled scoring surge in recent weeks, and after yet another goal against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night, he hit a mark last reached by Mario Lemieux more than three decades ago. With his 21st goal in the last 14 games, Gauthier became the first player to accomplish the feat since Lemieux in the 1992-93 season, and became the only American in NHL history to do so. He hit the mark with just under five minutes left in the first period against the Sharks, finishing off a power-play marker set up by Jackson LaCombe and Mikael Granlund to give his side a 3-0 lead. The only other players to score 21 in 14 games are Lemieux (1992-93 and 1988-89), Teeme Selanne (1992-93), Alexander Mogilny (1992-93), Bernie Nichols (1988-89) and Wayne Gretzky (1980-81, 1981-82, and 1983-84). Gauthier's run started on Oct. 29, when he potted two goals against the Buffalo Sabres. He went on to score back-to-back hat tricks against the Ottawa Senators and Vancouver Canucks, then grabbed two more against the Pittsburgh Penguins and St. Louis Blues over the course of his streak. With the majority of his goals — 19 of them — coming since the calendar turned to November, he may set the record for most goals in a calendar month in the coming days, with Selanne atop the ladder with 20. Gauthier is only the eighth player and second American to score 19 in a calendar month, and has two more games against the Los Angeles Kings on Nov. 27 and 28 to break the record. On the season, the 22-year-old has 23 goals — tied for the league lead with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers — and nine assists in 25 games.

It looks like the forward could miss some time, as post-game head coach Jon Cooper told reporters, including Manager of Media Relations Benjamin Pierce that he was “a little worried” and that he might be out for “a bit”. It’s not immediately clear where the injury happened but he exited during the second period, ending his night after just 6:34 on the ice. In a contract year the 27-year-old has stepped up in a big way, already at 13 points in 24 games when his career high is 22. Known to be a dependable shutdown winger, Holmberg has shown new elements to his game, being rewarded with time on the power play as well as a top six deployment, including tonight on Brayden Point ’s wing. Going 7-4-0 since star Nikita Kucherov ’s unexpected and league-shaking trade request , the Bolts lost to Carolina tonight and haven’t had the smoothest past few days. Last Sunday the superstar was benched in a convincing loss to Buffalo. Through it all, Holmberg has stayed in Cooper’s good graces, earning more shifts that night and continuing to cement himself as a vital middle-six role player. items.title: Canucks fall to Red Wings as Finnie, Arvidsson have three points each
items.body: DETROIT — Emmitt Finnie scored two early goals to lead the Detroit Red Wings to a 5-1 victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Wednesday night in a battle of last-place teams. Finnie added an assist and Viktor Arvidsson had a goal and two assists for Detroit, which had lost seven of eight. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher also scored and Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves. Vancouver had won three of five since breaking a 1-16-1 skid. Finnie got his first at 1:16, tipping in Arvidsson's shot from the right wing, then made it 2-0 at 4:05 by knocking in the rebound of Marco Kasper's shot. Finnie was the first Red Wings player to score twice in the first five minutes of a game since Brett Hull had two in the first 3:56 of a 5-2 win over the St. Louis Blues on Jan. 26, 2002. Hull finished that game with five points — three goals and two assists. Raymond made it 3-0 with a power-play goal with 57 seconds left in the first. Moritz Seider fed him the puck at the right faceoff spot, and he beat a screened Merilainen for his 10th goal of the season. Compher got Detroit's fourth goal at 6:24 of the second period, tapping in Michael Brandsegg-Nygard's pass at the back post. Paul Cotter ruined Tarasov's shutout bid with a goal at 7:26 of the third, but Arvidsson restored the four-goal lead at 8:08. Detroit outscored Vancouver 10-3 while sweeping the two-game season series.

items.summary: Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned to the Florida lineup in style, with Marchand getting three assists and Barkov scoring an empty-netter to help the Panthers beat the Ottawa Senators 5-3 on Wednesday night.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned to the Florida lineup in style, with Marchand getting three assists and Barkov scoring an empty-netter to help the Panthers beat the Ottawa Senators 5-3 on Wednesday night. Anton Lundell, Sam Bennett, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen also had goals for Florida, which got both Marchand and Barkov back after each missed nearly two months with knee injuries suffered in the season's opening week. It was Barkov's first home game for Florida since the final game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final. Jacob Markstrom stopped 25 shots. Dylan Cozens and Philip Tomasino had goals 41 seconds apart early in the second period for Ottawa, with Artem Zub and Jake Sanderson picking up assists on both as the Senators took a 2-1 lead. The rest of the game was all Florida, and Ottawa's nine-game point streak (7-0-2) came to an end. Michael Amadio scored with 51 seconds left for the Senators. Mikkola tied it for Florida midway through the second period and Marchand — stickhandling around a pair of Senators — set up Lundell for the goal that gave the Panthers a 3-2 lead going into the third. Bennett's goal with 10:43 left sealed it, beating Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark from close range for a 4-2 lead. The play started with Florida goalie Jacob Markstrom coming way out of the net, nearly to the blue line, to send a loose puck to the right-wing boards. Marchand played it to Lundell, who set up Bennett. Ullmark entered the game as the NHL's leader this season with a 1.44 goals-against average and a .938 save percentage. The Panthers solved him, becoming the first team to score four on Ullmark this season. In his first 13 appearances this season, Ullmark allowed three goals only once — in a 4-3 overtime win over Colorado on Nov. 12.

items.summary: Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night.
items.body: BOSTON — Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night. Kyle Connor and Josh Morrissey each had a goal for Winnipeg, which won its fourth straight road game and improved to 9-1-1 in its last 11 overall. Mark Scheifele, the Jets' career goals leader, added an empty-netter for the 381st of his career. Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten scored for the Bruins, who dropped the second of their season-high six-game homestand. Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 shots. Barron’s goal came with 2:07 left in the second when he poked the puck between Swayman’s pads to make it 3-2 after the goalie mishandled the rebound of Mario Ferraro’s shot. Boston’s Tanner Jeannot and Winnipeg’s Tyrel Bauer squared off in a lengthy fight midway into the opening period that featured numerous haymakers. Trailing in the second, Boston tied it at 2 when Minten, positioned directly in front of the net, tipped Mason Lohrei’s shot by Daws at 10:57. Morrissey’s slap shot from the slot beat Swayman and gave the Jets a 2-1 edge late in the opening period. Off since a 7-5 victory over Washington at home Saturday, the Bruins had tied it at 1 on Geekie’s power-play goal off a pretty pass across the front of the net by David Pastrnak at 6:11. Connor’s wrister from the left circle made it 1-0 just 65 seconds into the game. The Bruins won the first meeting between the teams in overtime on Oct. 2.

Maxim Tsyplakov and Brennan Othmann also each had a goal and an assist for the Flames, who snapped a three-game losing streak. Ryan Strome, Jonathan Castagna and Yegor Sharangovich also scored. Zayne Parekh had an assist to pass Miles Zaharko for the fifth-most points by a Flames’ defenceman younger than 21. Evgeni Malkin passed Bryan Trottier for 19th-most points in NHL history with a power-play goal and an assist for Pittsburgh. Malkin, who missed the last two games because of an injury, had his 382nd multipoint game and tied Teemu Selanne for fourth among players born and trained outside of North America. Rickard Rakell also had a power-play goal and Tommy Novak also scored. The Penguins scored two home power-play goals for the first time since an Oct. 3 win against Montreal. Arturs Silovs stopped 20 shots for the Penguins, who lost their fifth straight. Pittsburgh, last in the Eastern Conference, has lost 10 of 12 overall. The Flames won their 64th straight game when scoring four or more goals. They’re one four-goal win from tying the New York Rangers’ 65-game run from 2011-14, the longest mark in NHL history. No corresponding transaction was required, as he becomes the seventh defenseman on the roster. If he is able to get into a game it would be Kirsanov’s first NHL action. A lefty who stands at 6’2″, 220 lbs, he carries solid positioning and sufficient mobility as a nice piece to supplement a Kings blue line which could use some youth infusion, showing its age outside of Brandt Clarke . Looking to break through at the highest level, the Russian is actually older than Clarke, holding plenty of experience overseas with 120 games of regular season KHL experience as well as eight more playoff games under his belt. A product of the St. Petersburg SKA program in Russia, Kirsanov played for the KHL powerhouse early in his professional career, the same team Artemi Panarin represented before coming over to North America. items.body: Register Login Ducks Recall Laurent Brossoit By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 6:00 pm The Anaheim Ducks will have their oldest netminder back in the starters’ crease this evening. According to a team announcement , the Ducks recalled goaltender Laurent Brossoit from the San Diego Gulls in the AHL, and he will start tonight against the San Jose Sharks. Technically, tonight’s contest will be Brossoit’s first against his former team. Still, he didn’t have a lengthy history with the Sharks organization. In 2024, the Chicago Blackhawks signed Brossoit to a two-year, $6.6MM contract in free agency. Unfortunately, hip and knee injuries prevented him from playing a game with the Blackhawks. Chicago traded Brossoit to San Jose last January. By the time his contract ended, Brossoit had appeared in only one game with the Sharks. Regardless, he landed on his feet this past summer, inking a one-year, $1MM deal with the Ducks as their third-string netminder. On Halloween, after Anaheim had lost seven of their last eight contests, they recalled Brossoit to debut with the club. Although his save percentage (.867 SV%) and goals-against average (3.42) weren’t good, Anaheim won four of Brossoit’s five appearances, effectively turning their season around. Unfortunately, since Brossoit’s last start on November 11th, the Ducks are in a similar situation. They’ve lost five of their six matchups since Brossoit was reassigned. Every NHL season carries one question that fans seemingly can't get enough of: When will the next Canadian team win the Stanley Cup? items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google ARLINGTON, VA — The Capitals have had a rough start to the 2026-27 season, but the source of their problems is clear: defense. Since November 1, Washington has allowed an average of 5.11 goals per game , easily clearing the Chicago Blackhawks and Vancouver Canucks for worst in the NHL. Those defensive woes have been well-documented through the Caps’ now five-game losing streak, a skid they’ll look to break out of when they face the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday. But even as they struggle mightily to keep pucks out of their own net, they’ve had far less trouble scoring on opponents. The Capitals have averaged 3.22 goals per game, good for 15th in the league — not stellar, certainly, and likely somewhat the result of score effects, but a far cry from their metrics on the other end of the ice. Asked Wednesday whether the Caps have neglected their defense to chase offensive opportunities, head coach Spencer Carbery agreed wholeheartedly. Regardless of yesterday’s demotion, Warren should expect to hold down a long-term spot with the Ducks relatively soon. Anaheim lost multiple defenders this past offseason, and although he likely won’t contribute a ton offensively, Warren’s mobility, especially at his size, makes him a useful talent to have on the back end. Edvinsson brings a lot of things to an organization that is looking to trade for him. But one thing that has yet to be mentioned ties in with the December 1st deadline that looms over all this trade urgency. If Edvinsson doesn’t have an NHL contract by that date at 5 p.m. EST, he cannot play in the NHL for the 2026-27 season. What’s worse? Well, the longer he sits out, the more money he’ll cost the team looking to trade for him in year one of whatever deal he takes. In today’s day and age, it seems like a more than reasonable cap hit for any team that has been ponying up to trade for him, but his holdout makes that contract way more complicated in the short term. items.title: Babcock explains decision not to challenge possible Oilers goal vs. Vegas
items.summary: Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3.
items.body: Already down 2-0 early to the Vegas Golden Knights , the Edmonton Oilers got a puck past Carter Hart in the first period on Tuesday, but the play was ruled no-goal. The reason? Officials determined Oilers forward Mathieu Joseph had interfered with Hart on the play while battling for position with Vegas defenceman Rasmus Andersson . That left the Oilers with a choice. Do they challenge the ruling and try to cut the deficit in half or let the game play on? Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3. "Our guy went in on his own and then he bumped their stick," Babcock said after the game when asked about not challenging. "I haven't been back very long, but I've just learned they don't (overturn) anything. So unless you're 100 per cent sure, why be shorthanded?" Joseph said he didn't feel contact with Hart in the heat of the battle but conceded it was risky to challenge at that stage of the game. "It was a pretty tough call," Joseph said. "I was just trying to get in there. I feel like I'm getting pushed back a little bit ... Sometimes the bounces don't go your way, but you've got to stick with it."

items.body: Vegas moves closer in race with Edmonton after 'four-point swing' EDMONTON -- The battle between the top two teams in the Pacific Division lived up to its billing on Tuesday in what was the first encounter between the Vegas Golden Knights and Edmonton Oilers this season. What is quickly turning into a two-horse race got a little closer with Vegas pulling out a 5-3 win at Rogers Place to climb within three points of Edmonton for first place in the division. “That’s always the goal (to win division),” Vegas forward Mitch Marner said. “You know these games are never going to be easy, and every game matters. We’re happy with the win tonight. We try to take what we can out of this game, take the positives, learn from the negatives and get ready for the next one.” The Golden Knights (15-6-5) are on a good run as we approach Thanksgiving in the United States, having won two straight with a record of 6-1-4 in November. As a result, they have chipped away at the Oilers (17-6-4), who have lost four in a row (0-3-1). The San Jose Sharks are third in the Pacific, but they are 11 points behind Vegas with a record of 11-13-2. “It was a four-point swing and it’s obviously two really good teams going at it,” Vegas forward Nic Dowd said. “That’s a high-level team. They play really good hockey for three periods, and it’s good for us to understand that and come into this building and play that way and stay consistent with it regardless of the score. items.body: Longtime USA Hockey athletic trainer 'a glue guy' that is 'just awesome to be around' The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phi Kessel, TJ Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com staff writer William Douglas profiles Wong. When Stan Wong isn't tending to injured hockey players as a head athletic trainer, he's working at the Oriental Chow Mein Company, a Massachusetts business his family established after they immigrated from China more than a century ago. "Whether I'm a chow mein maker or an athletic trainer, I strive to be the best I can be, and I don't take that lightly," Wong said. "That's how much I push myself. That's what I expect." For more than 40 years, Wong given his best as a beloved head athletic trainer with the Washington Capitals (1986-99) and Florida Panthers (1999-2002), and for 59 United States teams in international competitions from world championships to the Winter Olympics. Wong's dedication to players, his professionalism and infectious personality are why the 68-year-old from Fall River, Massachusetts, is being inducted into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 30 in Washington, D.C. "I think the players look up to Stan as a considerate and trusted person," said John Vanbiesbrouck, USA Hockey assistant executive director of hockey operations and a 2007 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame inductee. "He's a glue guy that's around all the time. And some of the former (Team USA players), they're always asking, 'Where's Stan? Is he involved?' Most of the time we say, 'Yes, he is,' and they're very happy about that." "The Jets have become the 'Loveable Underdogs,' of the NHL," said author and Winnipeg Sun reporter Ty Dilello in an email. "It's an easy team to root for because -- no matter the obstacles -- they forge ahead." The Jets picked themselves up after a nine-game skid (0-7-2), dusted themselves off and started all over again after trading goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils on Oct. 23. They begin a three-game road trip at the Boston Bruins on Wednesday (7 p.m. ET; NESN, TSN3). "I'm very comfortable with what we accomplished over a period of time," Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said. items.body: National Hockey List names Ullmark, Schaefer, McDavid as great blessings Welcome to the National Hockey List. Each week, NHL.com senior writer Dan Rosen will provide a list dealing with important topics around the NHL. With Thursday being Thanksgiving in the United States, Rosen is giving one reason for fans of each team in the NHL to be thankful at this time of the year. Ottawa Senators: Be thankful for goalie Linus Ullmark , because you're a much different team when the Swede is in the net. They are 12-1-0 with 18 goals against when he plays, and 4-5-3 with 47 goals against when he doesn't. Tampa Bay Lightning: Be thankful for Nikita Kucherov , because you don't know how much longer you're going to have him. Kucherov is in the last year of his contract and reportedly has asked for a trade, though Lightning general manager Julien BriseBois said that is not going to happen. Maybe there's still hope fences can be mended and he stays in Tampa Bay beyond this season, but for now be thankful that you've got him there because he's a special, once-in-a-generation player. Montreal Canadiens: Be thankful for being well managed because it can keep a team a Stanley Cup contender for a long time. Give general manager Kent Hughes and president Jeff Gorton a lot of credit for managing the cap well and pulling the trigger on necessary trades, like the one Sunday to acquire Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings. That can only happen with excellent cap and roster management, and terrific amateur scouting. Boston Bruins: Be thankful that Elias Lindholm is healthy and has been a consistent offensive threat with 22 points (11 goals, 11 assists) in 23 games.
